inline.s: Filled with Dharma joy, nourished by the delight of Chan.

Question: Sitting meditation can improve the structure and function of the brain, boosting immunity, creativity, and quality of life. Moreover, the alpha brainwaves produced during meditation are highly effective for healing psychological trauma, transforming negativity, and dispelling anxiety, restlessness, and depression. As a result, it has drawn ever more attention, and some media have said: “Meditation awakens the mind and is sweeping Europe and America.” Because the practical benefits of meditation are supported by science, and with celebrities lending their voices to the wave, Time magazine reported that meditation has become fashionable in mainstream American society, with ten million adults meditating regularly (double the number ten years earlier). In my view, sitting in meditation through breath-based Buddha-recitation goes even further, cultivating both body and mind together. My question is: how does one sit in meditation through breath-based Buddha-recitation?

[Cultivating both nature and life] The comprehensive cultivation of body and mind. Cultivation of the body means health, longevity, and happiness; cultivation of the mind means awakening to the Way, attaining the Way, and ending birth and death.
Answer: First, let us assume that you have already mastered the method of breath-based Buddha-recitation. As for how to master the method of breath-based Buddha-recitation, see in detail
The Essentials of Breath-Based Buddha-Recitation
Second, please watch the video below on boosting alpha waves, to facilitate our discussion.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
In the video above, the “tuning” is done with the help of brainwave feedback technology to boost alpha (
α

) waves. In the actual meditation of breath-based Buddha-recitation, although you have none of these instruments, you can use the feedback signals obtained from observing your sensations to “tune” yourself: when you feel delight and light ease (something like the feeling of “a red sun rising in my heart”), this is the sign that alpha waves have appeared. Through continual practice and experimentation, you will master this method. Then, by using it often, you will grow more and more adept, until you can produce the same effect even while standing and reciting the Buddha’s name. Think how wonderful it is to practice breath-based Buddha-recitation like this amid nature! Master Yinguang said:

“When the Buddha’s name is raised, deluded thoughts entirely vanish. The whole body grows cool and clear, and the heart is filled with gladness — exactly like sweet dew poured upon the crown and ghee moistening the heart. This joy cannot be described by any comparison.”
(Record of the Marks of Buddha-Recitation Samādhi)

Besides healing body and mind and boosting immunity and creativity, the appearance of alpha waves has another important function: it keeps you cultivating with keen interest amid the delight of Chan and the joy of the Dharma, day after day, and so makes it easy to achieve “thought following thought without interruption, until repeated practice becomes second nature” — a reliable guarantee of rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[Repeated practice becomes second nature] Through repeated practice, one makes it instinctive.

Note: Brainwave feedback technology places eight electrodes on the trainee’s head (four on the left brain and four on the right, distributed from front to back) to receive brainwaves, then amplifies, filters, and decomposes them, and uses musical tones (flute, oboe, organ) as feedback signals for the trainee to listen to through headphones. The volume of the feedback music rises and falls with the energy of the α waves; if one or more regions suddenly generate an especially large amount of α waves, the flute sound changes into the oboe sound, and when α waves are generated synchronously in both the left and right brain, the feedback is expressed as the deep, rich sound of the organ. In this way the trainee comes to know the state of his own α waves, so that through his own continual experimentation, together with the trainer’s guidance over the intercom, he can find the way to boost α waves. This feedback music stops after lasting two minutes; then the computer screen before him lights up, displaying the feedback figures of α-wave energy at the eight electrodes (these figures are the square roots of the α-wave energy at each site). After these figures have been shown on the screen for eight seconds, they vanish, the screen darkens again, and the feedback music sounds once more. And so it alternates. The reason this article plays the video is to inspire how, through
feedback signals obtained from observing one’s sensations, one may “tune”
oneself to boost α waves.
Question: During my sitting I see various visions, some good and some bad. How should I deal with them?
Answer: The Diamond Sutra says:
“All that has marks is empty and false.”
Therefore, whether the visions are good or bad, beautiful or ugly, pay them no attention whatsoever —
“do not grasp at marks, but remain unmoved in suchness.”

(Diamond Sutra) These visions are all illusions produced by body and mind; do not take them as real and give rise to love or hate, grasping or rejecting, and still less should you deliberately pursue spiritual responses! In this way you will be free of the fault of being possessed by demons. If some vision keeps entangling you without cease, immediately open your eyes and look around: in broad daylight, how could such strange things exist! “See the strange and do not regard it as strange, and the strangeness will defeat itself.” At once step down from your seat, move your limbs, stretch yourself out, or pace slowly for a while, and then return to sit again.
